public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Coloring.EdgeLabeling

@[expose] public section

/-!
# Edge colourings of a SimpleGraph

`SimpleGraph.IsEdgeColouring H c` asserts that `c : ι → SimpleGraph V` is a partition of
the edges of `H` into colour classes indexed by `ι`. The classes must (1) cover `H`
(`H = ⨆ i, c i`) and (2) be pairwise disjoint (each edge belongs to exactly one class).

This unifies the previous local `IsNEdgeColouring` (`ι = Fin n`) and `IsCountableEdgeColouring`
(`ι = ℕ`) shapes used in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/596.lean`. The two are now special
cases of `IsEdgeColouring` parameterised by the index type.

`SimpleGraph.TopEdgeLabeling.CliqueFree` is the Ramsey-theoretic condition on the other
edge-colouring shape Mathlib provides, a labelling of the edges of the complete graph: no
colour class contains a clique of the given size.
-/

namespace SimpleGraph

/-- `IsEdgeColouring H c` asserts that `c : ι → SimpleGraph V` is a partition of the edges
of `H`: the colour classes cover `H` (`H = ⨆ i, c i`) and are pairwise disjoint. -/
def IsEdgeColouring {V ι : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph V) (c : ι → SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  H = ⨆ i, c i ∧ ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (c i) (c j)

/-- A labelling of the edges of the complete graph on `V` by `ι` is `n`-clique-free when no
colour class contains an `n`-clique, that is, when it admits no monochromatic `n`-clique. -/
def TopEdgeLabeling.CliqueFree {V ι : Type*} (C : TopEdgeLabeling V ι) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ι, (C.labelGraph i).CliqueFree n

end SimpleGraph

reformulations.difference: Represents an arbitrary Ramsey edge labelling by a family of spanning colour-class graphs, rather than by a function from the graph's edge set to the palette.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved in Lean, for arbitrary vertex and colour types: H.IsEdgeColouring c ↔ ∃ C : H.EdgeLabeling ι, ∀ i, C.labelGraph i = c i. Graph suprema are edge unions; coverage and pairwise disjointness give each edge exactly one label. Conversely, Mathlib's labelGraph families cover H and are pairwise edge-disjoint. Empty colour classes correspond to unused labels. Also proved translations of both universal and existential quantification over these representations, covering their uses in the Ramsey library.

reformulations.difference: Expresses absence of a monochromatic clique by requiring every label graph to be clique-free.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved in Lean that C.CliqueFree n is equivalent to ¬ ∃ (i : ι) (s : Finset V), s.card = n ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ hxy : x ≠ y, C.get x y hxy = i. This follows from Mathlib's pairwise-adjacency definition of a clique and its labelGraph adjacency characterization. The equivalence includes empty types and n = 0 or 1.

review.notes: Checked both declarations and all downstream uses, including the Ramsey predicates used by Erdős 596 and the triangle Ramsey definition used by Erdős 183. Experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/use_sites.lean both compile successfully. They cover empty/singleton vertex types and palettes, unused colours, coverage and overlap failures, and small clique sizes. Kernel-checked boundary lemmas give multicolourTriangleRamsey 0 = 2 and multicolourTriangleRamsey 1 = 3; the zero-colour extension does not affect either theorem in problem 183. The equivalence and boundary proofs contain no sorry or added axioms.
